title: Planes Still Have Ashtrays And It's Not An Oversight
hook: A fixture for a banned activity, kept because somebody will break the rule anyway.

cast.note: Gus is the regulator. Dry, unbothered, correct. The episode is not anti-rule; the rule is the smart one.

scenes.note: The contradiction up front: a NO SMOKING sign and an ashtray in the same frame.

beats.action: a lavatory door; a lit NO SMOKING sign above it
the sign pulses; a BANNED FOR DECADES label lands
camera tilts down to a small metal ashtray set into the door; it circles teal
the NO SMOKING sign holds lit above the door
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.note: Gus arrives with a clipboard. The ashtray is required equipment — stamp it, do not joke about it.

beats.action: a LEFTOVER? label appears over the ashtray and is crossed out
Gus stamps REQUIRED onto a checklist page
a grounded aircraft icon appears beside the checklist
Gus turns the checklist page and runs a finger down it
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.note: A held beat. The tone shifts here from oddity to seriousness.

beats.action: the frame clears to a plain field; the ashtray sits alone, small
the light cools; the ashtray holds still

scenes.note: The unavoidable human. Shown as a hand and a cigarette only — no character breaking the rule on screen.

beats.action: a lit cigarette appears in the lavatory cross-section
a question mark hovers over two possible destinations
the smoke curl thickens and drifts against the ceiling
beats.sync: secondary action — closes a pacing gap

scenes.note: The bad outcome, stated as a diagram. Restrained — a glow, not a fire.

beats.action: the cigarette drops toward a paper waste bin
the bin outlines coral; the paper inside begins to glow
the alternative draws beside it: the cigarette lands in the metal ashtray and goes out

scenes.from: It is not there for smokers
scenes.note: The reframe. Designing for the person who ignores you is the whole idea. Hard cut.

beats.action: the ashtray lights alone as the rest of the door greys out
Bill glances at it once and moves on down the aisle; hard cut
